images.seen: too small to judge detail; start anchor matches Cliopatria's Achaemenid, Kush, Scythia and Chinese blocks, plus the culture polities (Oshara, Jomon) Cliopatria lacks; nothing out of place

Achaemenid shape follows Cliopatria's 404 outline (no Egypt, no Ionia, Baluchistan and most of Sistan dropped); Gandara and Hindush drawn as vassal tints inside it; Egypt is the 28th Dynasty on the Nile only; Qedar and Lihyan plausible; nothing speckled

Italy is split into Etruscans, Umbri, Picentes, Sabines, Aequi, Volsci, Samnites, Lucanians, Taras, Messapii, Croton with Greek poleis on the coasts, richer than Cliopatria and coherent; Delian League holds the Ionian coast; Macedon, Paeonia, Odrysians fine

Chinese states match Cliopatria's pattern; Yue and Chu as Cliopatria; Yiqu is a big square block (Ordos, Ningxia, east Gansu from the page's description) and Qin is smaller than Cliopatria's; no holes
Jin is now drawn whole (750 cells) in 404; before the patch its land was blank grey that year
India: Shaishunaga (with Avanti and the Ganga plain), Kuru, Panchala, Matsya, Surasena, Asmaka, Hindush and Gandara vassal tints; no speckle, no hole

issues.what: Jin's -404 keyframe (Jiang and Quwo only, 32 cells) started one year before the partition, so about 730 cells of Jin land were ownerless for the whole of 404 although the page dates the division to 403
Four skipped Decelea events (unknown place 'Decelea'): the Spartan occupation of Attica 413-404 was missing from the map

Achaemenid Empire loses the Indus lands at -404 (ledger/31, 1313 cells, Baluchistan 1242) and the -404 keyframe drops Sistan and Baluchestan (519) and Libyan cells; Cliopatria's outline falls from 1957 to 323 of Pakistan's 3277 cells and from 690 to 171 of Sistan's 691 and stays there to -331. The dossier's own note says 'Page silent ... to be checked'

Ionia: the Delian League ledger gives it to the Achaemenids in 412, but the Achaemenid -404 keyframe says 'Ionia is still out until 387', so 49 Ionian cells go from Persian (412-405) to ownerless at -404 and come back only in the 383 keyframe

Yuezhi is born at -404 with 3115 cells (Xinjiang 2273, Gansu 842), the first year of Cliopatria's shape; the page gives no founding date and puts the Yuezhi in Gansu and the Tarim region 'during the 1st millennium BC'

After the 403 partition 342 former Jin cells (266 in Hebei, 43 Shanxi, 28 Shandong, 5 Beijing) stay ownerless to the end of the window: Wei is restricted to the Zhongshan core and Zhao 'without Handan until 386' by their dossiers. With Jin whole in 404 this now shows as a wei_-404 snap at -403 (removed 342) instead of a jin snap at -404; the cells at the end anchor are the same

Kuru: the -500 anchor holds 172 cells but all three keyframes (-600, -450, -404) resolve to 59 cells, so 113 Haryana cells vanish at -450 with no event. The surplus comes from the previous window (207 cells at -600)

Scythia -450 keyframe snap (519 added, 203 removed): the dossier itself dates the Istros border to c. 480 and the Ciscaucasia withdrawal to the 5th century; the year of the shape change is not pinned by a page

Egypt: the contest zones of 460-454 and 405-404 ('Lower Egypt' + 100 km round Memphis) include Matruh (466 cells of desert and coast); the 28th Dynasty keyframe at -404 drops 1581 desert cells to nobody

Size-rule conflicts: none reaches 300 cell-years (largest yan/zhao 118 at -403, Yan keeps Beijing, Tianjin and north Hebei); the smaller state won every pair that I looked at and the result is plausible (Greek colonies over the generic Greek shape, Taras, Croton, Messapii, Lucanians, Massalia, Akragas)

dossier_requests.what: identity.start (-404) is Cliopatria's first shape year, not a sourced founding; consider an earlier start or a note
dossier_requests.why: The page gives no 404 date: Chinese histories place the Yuezhi in Gansu 'during the 1st millennium BC', the Guanzi mentions the Yuzhi, and 'In the past, they lived in the region between Dunhuang and Qilian'. The map draws a 3115-cell state appearing out of nothing in 404

problems: Achaemenid east (for the orchestrator and the m0400-m0301 agent): Cliopatria's Achaemenid outline keeps only 318-323 of Pakistan's 3277 cells and 171 of Sistan's 691 from -404 to -331, and the compiled map follows it, so about 1300 cells of Baluchistan and Sistan (Gedrosia, Drangiana, Arachosia) are drawn ownerless for 74 years. The Achaemenid Empire page does not date any loss: its infobox puts the empire's east at 'the Hindu Kush and the western Indus basin' and its army list names Gandarans, Sarangae, Pactyes. No patch written (I could not source a date); an override of achaemenid-empire_-404 and of the -383..-331 keyframes would be needed together, across two windows, if the project decides to hold these lands.
The jin_-404 override (from -403 to -370, shape and end unchanged) starts in my window but lasts into m0400-m0301; that window should not override jin_-404 as well.

events/0 and events/1 resolve Decelea as the ring 8-25 km round Athens (the page gives no coordinates, only 'about 120 stadia from Athens' and 'control of rural Attica'); four cells are hatched 413-405 and the occupation closes at -404 as Athens falls. The four original Decelea events in the delian-league and peloponnesian-league dossiers stay skipped; the dossiers could be given a gazetteer-resolvable spec.
One WebFetch (Ionian_War) failed with url_not_found; 4 pages were read: Achaemenid_Empire, Partition_of_Jin, Decelea, Yuezhi (5 fetch calls). The status of Ionia from 412 to 387 stays unsettled.
No hierarchy.csv row in this window looked wrong (Macedon and Cyrene under the Achaemenids are drawn as vassals as the rows say; Cyrene's vassal tie runs to -404 in the compiled map).
The first Cliopatria compare at -500 (world) is too small to judge by eye; the regional images carry the review.
